typecheck._comment: dependsOn build, NOT the reverse. Both targets write into the same `dist/`: this one emits declarations there (outDir in tsconfig.lib.json) while the rollup build's delete-output plugin rmdir's it. Run concurrently by `nx run-many`, they race and the build dies with `ENOTEMPTY: directory not empty, rmdir .../dist/components`, roughly one run in ten. Ordering them this way also makes the published types deterministic: before, `dist/index.d.ts` was written by BOTH and the winner was whoever finished last. The reverse ordering (build dependsOn typecheck) is the one blocked by the TS resolver issue described on the build target. See README-BUG § Unconfirmed.

build._comment: typecheck excluded from dependsOn: TS bundler resolver fails when consuming `@dashforge/forms/dist/index.d.ts` (a 1-line `export * from "./src/index"` re-export) through nx's composite project chain. `nx run typecheck` separately works; `nx run-many -t test` works (it bundles types via vitest). Re-attach `typecheck` once the publishables' dist d.ts wrappers are switched to inline `export ...` (out of scope F3).

test-perf._comment: Runs the *.perf.test.tsx specs with their wall-clock budgets enforced as written (DF_PERF collapses the tolerance in src/test-utils/perfBudget.ts to 1x). Run it on a machine doing nothing else. The same specs also run inside `test`, where the budgets carry 4x headroom so contention cannot false-fail the gate. `perf.test` is a path substring filter, not a glob: vitest treats positional args as substrings.
